requirement: When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation in `requirements.index.chapter.default`.

**Obligations and the tests that check them**
- **Appended top-level chapter, "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, with the index table.**
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` checks that the last item is a top-level chapter. It asserts the name, the path, an empty `parent_names`, no leftover `{requirements-index}` text, and rows for requirement and example definitions.
  - `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters]` asserts the same name and path. It also asserts the content starts with `# Requirements index` and contains the `| Definition | Evidence |` table header.
  - `tests/repository.rs#fn[mdbook_preprocessor_renders_definitions_between_stdin_and_stdout]` checks the same behavior through the real `habeas mdbook` binary over stdin and stdout. It asserts the appended chapter's name, path and detail sub-items.
- **Created even when the book has no requirements or examples.** `default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters` runs with an empty book and with a prose-only book. In both runs it asserts that the index chapter is appended.
- **No standalone directive: a marker inside a code block is literal.** The `with_prose` variant of `default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters` puts `:::{requirements-index}` in a fenced code block. It asserts that the introduction content is unchanged and that a default index is still appended.
- **No source file or edit target.** All three unit tests and the binary test assert `index.source_path.is_none()`. The first two also assert that no `md/requirements-index.md` file is written to disk.
- **Section number is the largest numbered top-level chapter plus one, or 1 if none is numbered.**
  - **No numbered chapters:** `default_index_exists_even_without_definitions_or_numbered_chapters` asserts `[1]` for an empty book and for an unnumbered introduction.
  - **Numbered chapter present:** `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` has a top-level chapter numbered 2 and asserts `[3]`.
  - **Harder cases:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[default_index_number_follows_top_level_chapters_across_parts_and_unnumbered_chapters]` has a part title, a separator and an unnumbered appendix. Its numbered chapters are 2, 4 and 3, so the largest is not last, and a nested `4.10` child is also present. It asserts `[5]`, so it rules out counting items, taking the last chapter's number, or using nested numbers.

**Standalone-directive-present case.** The case where a directive is present, and so no default chapter is appended, is the parent `requirements.index.chapter`'s obligation ("When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive"). `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` already tests it, asserting that `book.items.len()` stays 3. I treated this as the parent's obligation, so it needs no test under the subject.

I found no gaps.

text: When a book contains no standalone `{requirements-index}` directive, `habeas mdbook` MUST append a new top-level chapter titled "Requirements index" at `requirements-index.md`, containing the index table, even when the book defines no requirements or examples. The generated chapter MUST have no source file or edit target. Its section number MUST be one greater than the largest numbered top-level chapter, or 1 when no top-level chapter is numbered.

An mdBook chapter MAY contain one standalone `{requirements-index}` directive with an empty body, opened by at least three colons and closed by at least as many. A book MUST contain no more than one such directive. `habeas mdbook` MUST render a requirements index listing all requirements defined in rendered chapters, each linking to its evidence detail page under {cite}`requirements.index.detail_pages`. When a directive is present, it MUST replace the directive with the index table; otherwise, it MUST generate the chapter specified by {cite}`requirements.index.chapter.default`.
